correctness.rationale: For any constant-fixing S the gradient matrix A=BSR determines the exact BV quotient norm as its maximal l1 column sum. For p=1, B S=(I+lambda B B^T)^-1 B and the irreducible M-matrix inverse has strictly positive entries and column sums below one. For p=2, symmetric S fixes exactly affine sequences; an all-column endpoint-span <=1 hypothesis forces S to fix e_n-e_1, contradicting its nonaffinity for n>=4, so a monotone single-jump signal has amplified BV. Direct symbolic inversion gives the exact n=3 and n=4 gradient matrices, checks the n=4 outer-column inequalities for both sign regimes, and obtains (1+12lambda)/(1+10lambda). check.py executed symbolically and at 105 exact rational parameter/dimension instances; these calculations are secondary to the analytic all-n argument.

value.rationale: Hodrick–Prescott/Whittaker smoothing is canonical finite-difference regularization; the practical distinction between penalizing curvature and controlling first-order total variation is a motivated stability question. The theorem determines a uniform no-go law for every positive smoothing strength and every length at least four, proves a natural first-size threshold, establishes the exact four-sample amplification, and isolates the more general self-adjoint affine-fixed-space obstruction. These are structural facts rather than arbitrary sample enumeration; they identify precise differences between first- and second-order regularization.
